tasks.title: safe_subtract uses addition instead of subtraction
tasks.problem_statement: The `safe_subtract` function in `mathkit/arithmetic.py` is using the `+` operator instead of `-`. All subtraction results are wrong. Fix the operator so the function correctly returns `a - b`.
tasks.test_context: test_safe_subtract_positive, test_safe_subtract_negative, and test_safe_subtract_zero all fail because the function adds instead of subtracts (e.g. safe_subtract(10, 3) returns 13 instead of 7).

tasks.title: integer_divide uses modulo instead of floor division
tasks.problem_statement: The `integer_divide` function in `mathkit/arithmetic.py` is using the `%` (modulo) operator instead of `//` (floor division). It returns remainders instead of quotients. Fix the operator.
tasks.test_context: test_integer_divide_exact and test_integer_divide_truncates fail because the function returns the remainder instead of the quotient (e.g. integer_divide(10, 2) returns 0 instead of 5).

tasks.title: clamp uses wrong comparison for upper bound
tasks.problem_statement: The `clamp` function in `mathkit/comparison.py` has a flipped comparison operator for the upper-bound check. Instead of clamping values above `high`, it clamps values below `high`. Fix the comparison so values above `high` are correctly clamped.
tasks.test_context: test_clamp_within_range fails because clamp(5, 0, 10) returns 10 instead of 5 (values below high are incorrectly returned as high). test_clamp_above_high fails because clamp(15, 0, 10) returns 15 instead of 10.

tasks.title: is_in_range uses or instead of and
tasks.problem_statement: The `is_in_range` function in `mathkit/comparison.py` uses `or` instead of `and` to combine its two boundary checks. This causes it to return True for values outside the range. Fix the logical operator.
tasks.test_context: test_is_in_range_below and test_is_in_range_above fail because the function returns True for out-of-range values (e.g. is_in_range(-1, 0, 10) returns True instead of False).

tasks.title: overlaps uses or instead of and
tasks.problem_statement: The `overlaps` function in `mathkit/ranges.py` uses `or` instead of `and` to combine its two interval checks. This causes non-overlapping intervals to be reported as overlapping. Fix the logical operator.
tasks.test_context: test_overlaps_false fails because overlaps(1, 3, 5, 7) returns True instead of False. The `or` operator makes non-overlapping intervals appear to overlap.

tasks.title: span_length subtracts one instead of adding one
tasks.problem_statement: The `span_length` function in `mathkit/ranges.py` uses `- 1` instead of `+ 1` in its closed-interval length formula. This produces lengths that are off by two. Fix the arithmetic operator.
tasks.test_context: test_span_length_normal fails because span_length(1, 5) returns 3 instead of 5. test_span_length_single fails because span_length(3, 3) returns -1 instead of 1.

tasks.title: mean uses floor division instead of true division
tasks.problem_statement: The `mean` function in `mathkit/statistics.py` uses `//` (floor division) instead of `/` (true division). This truncates fractional means to integers. Fix the division operator.
tasks.test_context: test_mean_fractional fails because mean([1, 2]) returns 1 instead of 1.5. Floor division truncates the fractional result.

tasks.title: median indexes mid+1 instead of mid-1 for even-length lists
tasks.problem_statement: The `median` function in `mathkit/statistics.py` uses `mid + 1` instead of `mid - 1` when averaging the two middle elements of an even-length list. This picks the wrong pair of elements. Fix the index offset.
tasks.test_context: test_median_even fails because median([1, 2, 3, 4]) returns 3.5 instead of 2.5. The function averages ordered[3] and ordered[2] instead of ordered[1] and ordered[2].

tasks.title: count_words splits on literal space instead of any whitespace
tasks.problem_statement: The `count_words` function in `mathkit/strings.py` uses `.split(" ")` instead of `.split()`. This counts empty strings between consecutive spaces as words. Fix the split call.
tasks.test_context: test_count_words_multiple_spaces fails because count_words("one  two  three") returns 5 instead of 3. Splitting on a literal space produces empty strings between consecutive spaces.

tasks.title: truncate adds suffix length instead of subtracting it
tasks.problem_statement: The `truncate` function in `mathkit/strings.py` uses `+ len(suffix)` instead of `- len(suffix)` when computing the slice endpoint. This produces output longer than max_length. Fix the arithmetic operator.
tasks.test_context: test_truncate_long fails because truncate("hello world", 8) returns "hello world..." instead of "hello...". The slice takes 11 characters instead of 5 before appending the suffix.
